mcqs.keyword: Key judgment and status of CEC
mcqs.question: What did the Supreme Court hold in T.N. Seshan v. Union of India (1995) regarding the Election Commission of India?
options: A multi-member Election Commission is valid, and the Chief Election Commissioner is not superior to the other Election Commissioners in decision-making.
The Election Commission is a single-member body, and the Chief Election Commissioner is superior to all other Election Commissioners in decision-making.
The Election Commission may conduct only elections to Parliament and State Legislatures, not elections for President and Vice-President.
The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only after approval by the Union Cabinet.
mcqs.explanation: In T.N. Seshan v. Union of India (1995), the Supreme Court upheld the validity of a multi-member Election Commission and held that the Chief Election Commissioner is not superior to the other Election Commissioners in decisions. The tempting opposite view is incorrect because the judgment did not make the Chief Election Commissioner superior to the other Election Commissioners.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Supreme Court’s decision in Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India (2023) is incorrect?
options: The committee included the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and the Chief Justice of India.
The committee was prescribed until Parliament makes a law on the subject.
The decision concerned the committee for recommending appointments to the Election Commission.
The committee included the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and the President of India.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is the one that names the President of India as a member of the committee. The committee comprised the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and the Chief Justice of India, and was to operate until Parliament makes a law.
